newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Steyr says wins Chrysler jeep deal.
newsitem.headline: Steyr says wins Chrysler jeep deal.

text.p: VIENNA, Dec 5 (reuter) - Austrian car maker Steyr-Daimler-Puch said on Thursday it had won an order to continue assembling Chrysler jeeps at its Austrian plant for an additional six years from 1999 to 2004.
In a statement Steyr said the deal would generate 10 billion schillings in agregate sales and require 1.6 billion schillings in investment.
Steyr said the order, which includes production of the new model of Chrysler's Jeep Grand Cherokee range, would result in the creation of an extra 400 jobs at its plant in Graz.
"This makes a significant contribution to securing the economic future of our plant into the new millenium," said Steyr chief executive Rudolf Streicher.
Steyr said it would assemble 390,000 vehicles at the rate of 65,000 a year, with the first due to roll off the production line on January 11, 1999.
"For our business the new Chrysler order means sales of 10 billion schillings which will generate significant added value," the Steyr statement said.

Chrysler Europe chief Timothy Adams said the deal would enable the company to meet growing demand for the Cherokee model. "In our strategy to raise the sale of Chrysler vehicles in Europe to 200,000 within one decade the Grand Cherokee is a very important model," he said.
Steyr said the additional 1.6 billion schillings in investment would be necessary to expand capacity in production, assembly and paintwork.
Steyr said it had also won an order worth 80 million schillings to help develop the new Grand Jeep Cherokee.
